newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistan sets GDP growth target at six pct.
newsitem.headline: Pakistan sets GDP growth target at six pct.

text.p: Pakistan's policy-making National Economic Council on Thursday set a gross domestic product (GDP) growth target of six percent for fiscal 1997/98 (July/June).

No official estimate of the growth for fiscal 1996/97 ending on June 30 was available, but economists fear it could be less than three percent because of the country's economic troubles while it has averaged six percent during the past 30 years.
"We will attempt a GDP growth rate of six percent" (in 1997/98), state Planning Commission deputy chairman Hafeez Pasha told a news conference after a council meeting in Islamabad.
Pasha said that in balance of payments, Prime Minister Nawaz Sharif's government planned to curtail the current account deficit to five percent of the GDP from an estimated seven percent this year.
The government has projected the value of exports to grow to $10.5 billion in 1997/98 from about $9 billion in 1996/97.

"If we achieve this growth rate...that will give us the kind of growth we need to sustain our balance of payments," he said. "In that way we can bring the current account deficit down by about $1 billion and at that rate it will be about $3.5 billion."

Pasha said an annual development plan approved for 1997/98 projected a production increase of five percent in agriculture, seven percent for manufacturing and six percent for services. He did not give the estimated figures for this year.
Wheat production is projected to increase to 18 million tonnes from a little more than 16 million tonnes estimated for 1996/97, he said.
